task:
Thoroughly update ALL user-facing documentation (README.md, docs/RUNBOOK.md, docs/GUIDED-MIGRATION.md, docs/MIGRATION-SCOPE.md, docs/HETEROGENEOUS.md) so that a NON-DEVELOPER ('a dummy') can use pgmig end-to-end with zero assumed knowledge. writeScope forbids touching code: every command and flag you document MUST exist in src/cli.ts - read it and conform to it exactly (command names, flags, defaults, confirm gates). Rules: do not weaken tests; no git ref mutations; PUBLIC repo - no internal company/customer/employee names, no incident IDs, no internal Slack/Notion links, no internal hostnames (the no-internal sensor enforces this every iteration).

1. README.md is the single entry point. Restructure/expand it to contain:
   a. WHAT pgmig is and the THREE use paths with a decision table: (A) near-zero-downtime migration via logical replication (the doctor -> bootstrap -> replicate -> watch -> reconcile -> cutover -> teardown pipeline), (B) rehearsal/sandbox, (C) Postgres major-version upgrade rehearsal (upgrade doctor -> capture -> lab -> verify). When to pick which.
   b. PREREQUISITES with exact check commands: Bun, Docker (for sandbox/lab/integration tiers), Postgres client tools (pg_dump/psql - local major must be >= the source server major, else a GSSAPI negotiation error), network reachability (direct db host vs pooler; logical replication needs the DIRECT connection; the direct host may be IPv6-only without the IPv4 add-on), optional SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN for provision/config-sync/sandbox.
   c. SETUP: clone, bun install, env vars table (SOURCE_DB_URL, TARGET_DB_URL, SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN and friends - where to find each value in a Supabase dashboard; empty-string means unset), a minimal ANNOTATED migrate.config.yaml example.
   d. QUICK START A (migration): the pipeline in order with copy-paste commands and short expected-output snippets; one line per step saying what it does; the preview/--confirm gates explained; exit codes.
   e. QUICK START B (upgrade rehearsal): upgrade doctor, upgrade capture, upgrade lab (--seed-gib for the no-production-data path, --capture-dir for the real one), upgrade verify - each with a working bash example in a fenced code block.
   f. COMMAND REFERENCE: every command in src/cli.ts (doctor, bootstrap, replicate, watch, reconcile, cutover, teardown, verify, translate, provision, config-sync, storage, sandbox up/down/status, rehearse + subcommands, status, preflight, drift, upgrade doctor/capture/lab/verify) with a one-line purpose and a working example in a bash code block. The docs-examples sensor requires EVERY command to appear inside a fenced bash code block.
   g. TROUBLESHOOTING table (symptom -> cause -> fix) covering at least: GSSAPI/old pg_dump client, pooler vs direct IPv6 connection, auth.users FK row rejections (session_replication_role), md5-password roles cannot connect post-upgrade, extension version mismatch, WAL retention/disk pressure from the replication slot, capacity failures at project creation, pg_cron jobs firing on a half-migrated target (pause at watermark; nothing on target until cutover), vault/pgsodium root key not carried by dump/restore, slow initial copy caused by STORED generated columns (~7x, measured), permission errors and the unprivileged-user path.
   h. SAFETY MODEL: read-only by default, the confirm gates, the rollback point of no return (lossless until the app is repointed), where logs are written (logs/).
2. docs/RUNBOOK.md: sync with the CURRENT cli.ts (commands, flags, defaults - fix any drift), and make the cutover-day checklist include the safety-net items: named restore point via the Management API before the freeze, target-region capacity re-check at instance size, cron paused at the watermark, pg_cron/pg_net disabled on the target until cutover, re-password custom login roles, storage copy method per S3-protocol setting, JWT secret/API keys never copied (sessions invalidate, env vars change).
3. docs/GUIDED-MIGRATION.md: verify every command/flag against src/cli.ts and fix drift; reference the migration doctor's warnings (generated columns, cron.job, vault root key, client version) where the walkthrough should watch for them.
4. docs/MIGRATION-SCOPE.md and docs/HETEROGENEOUS.md: accuracy pass only - fix anything contradicted by src/cli.ts or src/*; do not restructure.
5. STYLE: numbered steps, exact copy-paste commands, expected-output snippets, define every acronym on first use, 'if you see X, do Y' phrasing. No marketing prose. Assume the reader has never used psql, Docker, or a replication slot.

After all edits run 'bun run check'. The judge sensor (a second model playing the role of a non-developer following ONLY the docs) must pass - write for that reader.

sensors.name: docs-examples
sensors.cmd: awk '/^```(bash|sh|shell)/{f=1;next} /^```/{f=0} f' README.md docs/*.md > /tmp/pgmig-docblocks.txt; for c in doctor bootstrap replicate watch reconcile cutover teardown verify translate provision config-sync storage sandbox rehearse status preflight drift 'upgrade doctor' 'upgrade capture' 'upgrade lab' 'upgrade verify'; do rg -q --fixed-strings "$c" /tmp/pgmig-docblocks.txt || { echo "NO CODE-BLOCK EXAMPLE: $c"; exit 1; }; done
sensors.hint: every CLI command must appear inside a fenced bash code block in README.md or docs/ (prose mentions do not count) - add working examples for the missing ones, matching src/cli.ts flags exactly

sensors.name: no-internal
sensors.hint: an internal/sensitive term or link leaked into the docs (pattern list lives outside the repo) - remove it; the repo is PUBLIC

sensors.name: links-valid
sensors.cmd: for f in README.md docs/*.md; do d=$(dirname "$f"); rg -o '\]\(([^)#]+)' -r '$1' "$f" | while read -r t; do case "$t" in http*|mailto:*|\{*) continue;; esac; [ -f "$d/$t" ] || [ -f "$t" ] || { echo "broken link in $f: $t"; exit 1; }; done || exit 1; done
sensors.hint: a relative markdown link points at a file that does not exist - fix the target or the link

sensors.name: judge-dummy
sensors.cmd: bun ~/.pi/agent/skills/self-correcting-loop/judge.ts --model openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 --base HEAD --spec 'Acceptance criteria for pgmig documentation (README.md + docs/*.md). Judge as a NON-DEVELOPER who has never used psql, Docker, or replication slots, following ONLY these docs: (1) They can go from prerequisites to a completed migration: every step has a copy-paste command in a fenced code block, expected output, and where-to-find-each-value guidance for env vars. (2) The pipeline order is correct per src/cli.ts: doctor -> bootstrap -> replicate -> watch -> reconcile -> cutover -> teardown, and the confirm/preview gates are explained. (3) The upgrade rehearsal group (upgrade doctor/capture/lab/verify) is documented with working examples. (4) Spot-check at least 10 documented commands/flags against src/cli.ts - ALL must exist with matching flags. (5) Troubleshooting covers: GSSAPI/old client, IPv6/pooler vs direct, auth.users FK, md5 roles, extension version mismatch, WAL disk pressure, cron on target before cutover, vault root key, slow copy from generated columns. (6) README, RUNBOOK and GUIDED-MIGRATION are mutually consistent (same commands, same order). (7) No internal names, incidents, or internal links anywhere.'
